PRACTICE FIELD GUIDE / INTERACTIVE EDITION

A good fee.
A better margin.

Understand what a consulting engagement earns once the hidden hours—and the value of your time—are included.

Practice Editorial · Consulting profitability calculator

PRICE THE WHOLE ENGAGEMENT

Revenue is the beginning of the calculation.

A project can look attractive on the proposal and feel very different after the preparation, revisions and administration are counted. This calculator makes those assumptions visible before you commit.

Use it to explore one engagement, compare a change in scope, or check how much room the fee leaves after valuing your time. All amounts are in pounds sterling and exclude VAT and tax.

READ THE RESULT

Three numbers.
Three different questions.

Project surplus

What remains after project costs, allocated overhead and the internal value of your hours. This is a planning estimate, not your bank balance or statutory accounting profit.

Margin after time cost

How much of the project fee remains as that surplus. A negative margin means the fee does not cover all the assumptions you entered.

Effective earnings before time cost

What is available per hour after direct costs and overhead, before subtracting your chosen hourly time value. Compare this with the rate you want your work to support.

KEEP THE INPUTS HONEST

Useful estimates start with clear boundaries.

  • Count preparation, sales, meetings, revisions and administration alongside delivery.
  • Allocate overhead consistently. Do not include the same expense in both overhead and direct costs.
  • If your own pay is already included in project costs, avoid counting it again through the hourly time value.
  • This model assumes the fee is collected in full. It does not model tax, VAT, financing, bad debts or payment timing.
  • Try a second scenario with more hours or lower fees to understand how sensitive the result is.

THE NEXT CONVERSATION

Make scope and economics
part of the same decision.

If the estimate is uncomfortable, revisit the fee, the scope or the delivery approach before agreeing the engagement.

Talk about your practice ↗

Private interactive article · Not published

interactions.fallbackHtml:
A WORKED EXAMPLE · ALWAYS AVAILABLE

A £6,000 engagement, in plain numbers.

Start with a £6,000 fee. Subtract £600 of direct costs and £300 of allocated overhead: £5,100 remains before valuing your time. Delivery takes 40 hours and sales and administration take another 10 hours.

At an internal time value of £60 per hour, those 50 hours cost £3,000. The estimated project surplus is therefore £2,100, or 35% of the fee. Effective earnings before deducting that time value are £102 per hour. The break-even fee is £3,900.

Formula: surplus = fee − direct costs − allocated overhead − ((delivery hours + sales/admin hours) × internal hourly time value).

Margin = surplus ÷ fee. Effective earnings before time cost = (fee − direct costs − allocated overhead) ÷ total hours. A zero fee has no defined margin; zero hours has no defined hourly rate.
